**NEW FINDING**

FINDING_ID: F006
SEVERITY: 0.65

FIND: The `section_terminator` regex (line ~109) uses only `re.MULTILINE` as its flags, while the `marker_match` regex (line ~100) uses `re.IGNORECASE | re.MULTILINE`. This inconsistency means the parser is case-flexible when *locating* the ADMISSIBILITY block but case-rigid when *terminating* it. If a model uses mixed-case or title-case section headers (`Novelty:`, `Verified:`, `Corroboration:`), the section_terminator fails to match, and the admissibility `block` variable consumes all subsequent text until the next ALL-CAPS header or end-of-string. Evidence: line 109 `re.MULTILINE` vs line 100 `re.IGNORECASE | re.MULTILINE` — direct inspection.

FOLLOW: When `block` over-consumes, gate-pattern `re.search` (which uses `re.IGNORECASE`) scans through text from subsequent sections (NOVELTY, CORROBORATION, etc.). This compounds with C0014's cross-contamination mechanism: if downstream section text contains a gate name followed by a status word (e.g., `"q_retest: PASS was verified"`), the gate match will find it and produce a false positive (gate marked as PASS when it wasn't actually reported). More commonly, `block` simply contains extra noise text that doesn't match any gate pattern — benign but wasteful. The worst case is silent wrong results: a gate reported as PASS or FAIL based on text from a *different section entirely*.

ANALYSE: HARD — correctness constraint. The parser must terminate the admissibility block at the correct boundary. A case-sensitivity gap that causes the block to extend into other sections produces silently wrong parse results. This is not preference — it is functional correctness of the text parser. CONFIRMED: the inconsistency is visible by direct code inspection.

In practice, prose lines like `"the fix addresses..."` start with `"the"` not `"fix"`, and the `^\s*` anchor prevents mid-line matches.
